Maya R: Quick question — running partial per-layer quant (exclude embed/lm_head) and saw a perf regression on long sequences after calibration sweep. cc @Jon P @Kai L
perf-bot: Perf CI: regression detected (throughput -12%) on model rwin-13b-partial-quant at 1768923456 — benchmark: long-docs-suite
Jon P: can you paste the quant_plan + minimal perf numbers?
Maya R: pasted below, trimmed. calibration = symmetric, clip=0.995
```
layers: [
  0: fp16 (embedding)
  1: int8
  2: int8
  3: 4bit
  4: 4bit
  ...
  46: int8
  47: fp16 (lm_head)
]
profiling (seq=1024, batch=1):
  total tokens/s: 180
  baseline (all fp16): 320 tokens/s
  hot layers: attn_kv (layers 20-28) heavy dequant calls
  observed extra memcpy in KV path
```
Kai L: interesting — two suspects: (1) kernel selection fallback for small GEMMs -> ends up using fp16 path for some 4-bit-backed layers, (2) KV cache memory layout causing extra quant/dequant on append paths.
Sophia M: I've seen this before: when embeddings/lm_head excluded, scale factors shift and calibration rescales some intermediate FCs aggressively -> more zero-point churn for affine kernels which triggers slower code path.
Jon P: can you run a quick microprofile to show which kernel impl is picked? `RUNTIME_DEBUG=kernel:trace ./bench --model rwin-13b --quant-plan q.json`
Maya R: ran that, snippet:
```
[kernel-trace] layer 3: chosen_kernel=gemm_fp16_tiled (matrix M=64, K=512)
[kernel-trace] layer 4: chosen_kernel=gemm_int8_swp (M=128, K=256)
[cache-trace] kv-append: quantize->memcpy->dequantize sequence triggered for sharded-kv path
```
Kai L: so layer 3 is falling back to fp16 kernel despite being 4-bit designed — probably because M/K shape doesn't match int8/4bit fast path thresholds. We should add a small kernel selector rule: prefer int8/4bit kernels when K >= 256 and M <= 256 for our transformer blocks.
Maya R: agreed. also noticed calibration used global clip 0.995 — might need per-layer clip for layers with heavy outliers (head projections). per-layer clip reduces saturation and avoids weird scale blowups.
Sophia M: note on KV: when using sharded KV across devices, we do quantize at device boundary then dequantize at the aggregator which kills throughput. Two options: (A) keep KV in fp16 for layers where cache hits are >20% (fast path), (B) move quantization after KV concat so append doesn't do per-step dequantize.
Jon P: option B seems cleaner but involves changes to memlayout. Can we do A as a quick win — detect hot KV layers and force fp16 for them (even if rest is quantized)?
Maya R: I ran a quick ablation: force fp16 on kv-sensitive layers (20-28) + embeddings/lm_head excluded -> tokens/s = 210 (vs 180), quality delta <0.2% on perplexity. Still slower than baseline but much better.
perf-bot: Canary benchmark after temporary kv-fp16 patch: throughput +17% relative to regressed run, overall -6% vs all-fp16 baseline.
Kai L: next steps: (1) add kernel-selector rule to runtime for small/odd shapes, (2) add per-layer calibration pass that reports outlier ratio and suggests clip thresholds, (3) add KV hot-layer detector to auto-exclude from quant during runtime.
Jon P: for rollout we should A/B: canary group with `quant_plan_v1` (kv fp16 + kernel-rule) and `quant_plan_v2` (per-layer clip + partial 4-bit) and monitor token-RT and eval-set quality. If quality regresses >0.5% on long-docs prompts, auto-fallback.
Maya R: I'll run the two canaries tonight against long-docs and conversational eval sets and post results in the morning. Leaving notes in the PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/rt/quant/PR-342
Sophia M: adding note — watch out for lm_head scale mismatch when you re-enable fp16 there; we need a final rescale step at output stage if mixing types.
Maya R: thanks everyone, will follow up with numbers. :thumbsup:
